description: I’m Rithvi, the solo founder of EXPLONAUT+, driven by curiosity about exploring another world. Combining my interests in space science, AI, coding and design, I use NASA’s open data to explore how people could plan missions on Mars. EXPLONAUT+ embraces “The Next Frontier” by turning ambitious questions into working prototypes, testing assumptions and making complex decisions easier to understand through tools others can inspect and explore. Every idea begins with a question worth testing.
summary: Which discovery would you give up to leave enough time for the journey home?EXPLONAUT+ is a Mars surface mission-planning and decision-support platform that helps users choose where to go, which science activities to complete, and how much time to keep for the journey home. It combines NASA’s MRO HiRISE terrain and imagery with Perseverance’s archived locations in Jezero Crater, bringing observations from two missions into one interactive planning view. Users set their time budget, walking speed, slope limits, activity priorities, and reserve. The platform compares routes, activity combinations, and visiting orders to select the highest-scoring plan that fits those assumptions. Its disruption laboratory lets users simulate slower walking, extra fieldwork, or a blocked route, then see which objectives remain achievable. In a 105-minute scenario, a two-stop plan requires 95.2 minutes; a slowdown and fieldwork delay increase this to 120.2. Replanning selects one stop requiring 69.5 minutes, including reserve. Route comparisons, timelines, shareable scenarios, and downloadable mission briefs make each decision understandable and reproducible. EXPLONAUT+ turns NASA observations into visible trade-offs between scientific ambition and return constraints. Independent calculation checks support the software; activities and disruptions are scenario assumptions, and operational astronaut safety remains unvalidated.
details:
A Marswalk has a one-time budget. Every additional journey or activity leaves less time for another objective or the return to base. EXPLONAUT+ helps users choose an itinerary, test changing assumptions, and understand why the plan needs to change.

WHAT WE DEVELOPED:

EXPLONAUT+ is a working Mars surface mission-planning and decision-support platform covering approximately 2.07 × 2.07 kilometres of Jezero Crater. It combines MRO HiRISE elevation and orbital imagery with Perseverance’s archived locations, connecting observations from two NASA missions in one interactive planning view.

Users explore relief, slope and imagery layers, choose science activities, and set their time budget, walking speed, slope cutoff, activity priorities and reserve. The platform compares enabled stop combinations and visiting orders, selecting the highest-scoring itinerary that fits those assumptions.

WHEN A PLAN STOPS FITTING:

In a 105-minute scenario, the planner selects stops A and C. Travel, activities and a 20-minute reserve require 95.2 minutes. A 20% walking slowdown and 15-minute fieldwork delay increase that requirement to 120.2 minutes.

Replanning selects stop A alone, requiring 69.5 minutes, including reserve. The user can see the consequence directly: one objective is dropped, and the revised excursion fits the specified disruption.

The disruption laboratory also allows users to mark synthetic exclusions on the map. The application recalculates routes around those cells and reassesses which activities remain achievable. These are planning scenarios, not detected hazards or live emergency navigation.

HOW IT WORKS:

An eight-neighbour Dijkstra search calculates shortest three-dimensional grid paths between the base and candidate stops. It excludes missing terrain, slopes above the selected cutoff, and user-blocked cells, while preventing diagonal shortcuts through blocked corners.

Required time includes the complete round trip, activity durations, and reserve. Disruption mode applies the reduced walking speed and one extra fieldwork allowance. The planner selects the highest scenario activity score within the budget, using shorter nominal duration to break ties.

Route comparisons, a modeled timeline and a time-versus-activity-points frontier expose the alternatives. Shareable scenario links preserve the inputs and exclusions. Downloadable mission briefs record sources, assumptions, and results. Activity points express planning priorities, not measured scientific value.

NASA DATA AND SCIENCE CONTEXT:

MRO HiRISE digital terrain model DTEEC_045994_1985_046060_1985_U01, version 1, supplies elevation. Its associated georeferenced orthoimage supplies the imagery layer. Mars 2020 PLACES records provide Perseverance’s historical positions.

Elevation at approximately 1.01-metre source spacing is aggregated into a 128 × 128 planning grid with approximately 16.15-metre cells. Native-resolution slope maxima control exclusions, and cells require at least 95% valid elevation coverage. Rover coordinates are transformed into the terrain projection and snapped to planning cells, with placement offsets disclosed.

Stop A represents Perseverance’s sol-116 viewpoint for imaging the layered Artuby outcrop from 615 metres away. The marker identifies the viewpoint, not the outcrop. Its proposed activity is remote imaging to examine visible layering. Stops B and C are archived traverse positions used for proposed surface documentation and comparative imaging.

Activities, durations, priorities, and reuse of the landing position as a habitat remain scenario assumptions.

CREATIVE CONTRIBUTION AND INTENDED BENEFIT:

EXPLONAUT+ connects terrain routing with activity selection under one return budget. NASA observations affect the route, route distance affects available fieldwork time, and changed assumptions affect the objectives selected.

The distinctive interaction is an inspectable decision: users can see what no longer fits, what the revised plan sacrifices, and how much time remains. This supports students, educators and researchers exploring simplified mission-planning scenarios. Educational and operational benefits have not yet been measured.

VERIFICATION:

Automated tests cover known-grid distances, missing terrain, blocked corners, independent route-segment summation and budget arithmetic. Additional checks cover synthetic exclusions, an impassable barrier, disruption feasibility, and a reserve exceeding the available budget.

A separate Python shortest-path implementation reproduced the default JavaScript route within 1e-6 metres. A recorded independent GDAL slope comparison covers 4,186,116 native interior pixels, with a maximum difference below 0.000008 degrees. These results support calculation consistency, not physical measurement precision or astronaut performance.

The evidence page provides verification records, source references, and provenance hashes. The downloadable source package includes the application and reproduction instructions.

TOOLS AND DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Canvas power the browser application. Python, NumPy, Pillow and GDAL support terrain processing and verification. Node.js runs software tests. OpenAI Artifact Tool supports the presentation, and ReportLab produces the PDF. No specialist hardware or user registration is required.

The design prioritises source traceability, understandable comparisons and clear separation between observations, calculations and assumptions. ChatGPT/OpenAI Codex assistance is acknowledged in the project materials.

LIMITATIONS:

The model assumes constant walking speed and symmetric travel. Its coarse grid cannot resolve every obstacle or narrow passage, and historical observations do not establish current Mars conditions. Validated suit physiology, oxygen use, fatigue, energy, weather, radiation, communications, and loose-ground mechanics remain outside the model.

User testing and external astronaut-mobility validation remain outstanding. EXPLONAUT+ is a research and education prototype and does not certify operational astronaut safety.
